intro: Here stands Erzurum Castle, a castle and walls in Erzurum province dating from the 5th century AD. Its inner citadel was founded under Theodosius, and the Tepsi Minaret, added by the Saltukids, still serves as the city's clock tower.
history: The inner citadel was founded under Theodosius in the fifth century, and for fifteen hundred years it stayed at the centre of the city's defence. Later, under the Saltukids, the Tepsi Minaret was added. In time it was put to use as a clock tower, and it has served that way ever since.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Tepsi Minaret, the citadel mosque, the curtain walls and the watchtower.
facts: Did you know? The clock movement in the Tepsi Minaret was brought from England in the nineteenth century, and locals came to call the minaret simply the clock tower. The inner citadel itself was founded under Theodosius in the fifth century AD.
outro: This brings our tour of Erzurum Castle to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for walking with us, and enjoy your visit.
